purpose: Map of the SocratexAI global AI core. Read this first; open only the entry you need.

layers.defaults: defaults/RULES.md + defaults/STYLE.md: always loaded for Claude and Codex
layers.local: local/: private, gitignored owner profile and patterns (created from local.example/)
layers.project: each project's INDEX.json, AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md and optional .ai/ overrides

Always-loaded rules shared by Claude Code and Codex in every project.
How Claude and Codex report to the owner in chat; overrides other report formats.
Engineering standard for writing and reviewing code in any language; the project's own standard wins on conflict.
When and how Claude and Codex commit, push and squash.
One flow per task type (feature, bug, refactor, review, docs, big task) with research gate, closure evidence and file-based handoff for large work.
Before trusting or reporting a measured number (FPS, latency, speedup, eval result): decide first, find the limiter, rule out a wrong measurement.
What to run and check before reporting a change as done.
How to choose between implementations and when to do the better version now.
Which model and effort to use, when to delegate or escalate, risk-based verification and the outcome log.
Backup, consent and rollback rules for changing agent configuration on this machine.
Short security checklist for business and client projects; run only when a change touches auth, secrets, payments, user input or external endpoints. Not for game projects.
When to just do it, when to plan first, when to research first and when to ask.
Verbatim detail bullets from defaults/RULES.md (named solutions, repeated fixes, skill learnings, context economy, finishing); the startup file keeps one short line per topic.
Short record for a choice that future work must not casually undo.
Frontmatter and layout for any rule document, guide or knowledge note, so scripts can index it and agents can skim it.
Template for one stage of a multi-stage pipeline with a human review after each stage (numbered folders, contract, output handoff).
Portable knowledge base and dated findings log on working well with AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex).
Comparison of our AI core with pstack (poteto) and Everything Claude Code (ECC); what to borrow, what not to install.
Jedna strona o tym, co odpalać i kiedy - tabela głównego flow, kolejność warstw, komendy sox i mapa katalogów (generowana z danych)
How to open the SocratexAI notes in Obsidian as a viewer and graph; optional, off by default.
Standardowy format nadpisań SocratexAI per projekt - które pliki, jakie klucze, reguły scalania i przykłady
Risk-based verification levels (LIGHT/STANDARD/FULL) and a learning loop that tunes model routing from logged task outcomes.
Operational notes for a Claude Code setup that AI-PRACTICES does not cover - usage metrics, session hygiene, settings, memory conventions, monthly review, self-growth safety.
Claude Code additions to the shared core (subagents, hooks, environment, tools); imported by the generated ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md.
Claude Code mod that draws an animated graph of Claude's work (you, Claude, sub-agents, tools, MCP, skills) with the 5-hour limit growth and a per-path cost estimate in a side panel.
Codex additions to the shared core; modules/tools/scripts/install.py concatenates core rules, this file and the local profile into ~/.codex/AGENTS.md.
🧭 <Project> agent rules
Claude notes for <Project>
Each place where {{name}} differs from the SocratexAI defaults, with the reason
Pointers to the business reasons behind {{name}}; mark gaps instead of guessing
Facts about the {{name}} project (stack, zones, layout, secrets policy)
Planowanie w trzech tanich etapach (formularz, research, sprawdzenie interpretacji) na wspólnym schemacie rejestru i wspólnym runnerze z pipeline'em review.
Ready patch for core/safety.json and claude/hooks/guard.py so the agent can edit knowledge documents but not config files in local/projects and local/groups
Jedno miejsce prawdy o projektach (zasady, wiedza, tickety, odstępstwa od standardów) w SocratexAI/local, z deterministyczną kolejnością czytania i trybem referencji
Docelowa struktura repo, kolejność nadpisywania, flow jako dane i plan migracji bez przerwy w działaniu
Rozkład wielkości zmian z realnych commitów i uzasadnienie min_changed_lines oraz max_chunk_lines.
Rejestr tanich, oskryptowanych sprawdzaczy (po jednym na zagadnienie), które tylko zgłaszają; poprawki robi jeden wykonawca; zbiera osobna sesja.

data.what: Schema of one SocratexAI config layer file (defaults, adapter, local overrides, project, project-private)
Schema of one extension manifest (modules/extensions/<name>.json shipped, local/extensions/<name>.json owner's), id socratex-extension/v1
Schema, fact table and condition grammar of the flow table (defaults/flow.json and its per-layer overrides), id socratex-flow/v1
Schema of local/groups/<group>/group.json: identity of a group of projects that share rules and config
Schema of one module manifest (modules/<group>/<name>/module.json), id socratex-module/v1
Schema of one preference index (defaults/preferences/<name>/<name>.json), id socratex-preferences/v1: which documents to load for a kind of work, and when
Schema of one profile file (defaults/adapters/<name>.json), id socratex-profile/v1; `config` is a bundle of config values validated by core/config.schema.json (without `profile`)
Schema of defaults/project-check.json: the rules `sox project check` applies to a project
Schema of local/projects/<key>/project.json: identity, group and knowledge place of one project
Named safety rules enforced by claude/hooks/guard.py; an owner layer relaxes one with safety.allow: [id]
Schema of core/safety.json: the named safety rules the guard hook enforces
Registry of review micro-checkers (one concern each). A project may add, disable or retier them in .ai/review.json. Spec: docs/specs/review-pipeline/SPEC.md
socratex-review-findings/v1

Registry of planning micro-checkers. Stage 1 (questions) is the normal AskUserQuestion form led by the main session and has no entry here. A project may add, disable or retier entries in .ai/planning.json. Spec: docs/specs/planning-pipeline/SPEC.md
socratex-directives/v1
socratex-risk-rules/v1
socratex-model-routing/v1
Shipped default values of the layered config (lowest layer, read by core/core.py)
The only place with the order of work steps: if (facts) then (stage, role, rule, gate, tool, ask). Facts and grammar: core/flow.schema.json
socratex-project-check/v1
Main agent plus a second agent (Codex) as subcontractor for search, tests and second-opinion review; opt-in only
Default: one main agent (the one using SocratexAI), no second agent; review and planning stay on
Duo (main agent plus second agent) plus relaxed safety rules (ids from core/safety.json); only an owner layer may select it
Engineering standard for writing and reviewing code
When and how to commit, push and squash
Reply profile for reports and answers to the owner
Machine-readable list of AI workflow improvements and their status

skills.name: gpt-share-read
skills.what: Read a public ChatGPT conversation link (chatgpt.com/share/...) or a saved HTML of such a page and extract its messages as Markdown or JSON. Use whenever the owner pastes a GPT/ChatGPT link and wants it read, summarized, searched or continued. Do not use WebFetch or a browser for these links.

skills.name: memory-review
skills.what: Monthly review of agent memory, scripts, skills and rule documents - merges duplicates, flags stale or unused items, asks the owner in one form what to change. Use on /memory-review or when the owner asks to clean up memory or tidy the tools.

skills.name: skill-reflect
skills.what: Turn logged skill learnings (LEARNINGS.jsonl next to each skill) into small owner-approved edits of SKILL.md. Use on /skill-reflect, during memory-review, or when skill_learn.py reports a skill as READY. Not for writing new skills from scratch.

skills.name: spec
skills.what: Interview with one form before non-trivial work, ending with a SPEC.md file (goal, out of scope, decisions, acceptance criteria, edge cases, verification). Use on /spec or when a task is larger than about an hour, touches architecture, data, saves, payments or auth, or the requirements are unclear. Not for small fixes or one-off scripts.

skills.name: token-efficient-code
skills.what: Select locally installed RTK, ast-grep, Serena, Graphify, TOON and Repomix for bounded code retrieval, CLI output reduction and context exports when the task benefits from those operations. Follow the active project workflow and preserve original verification evidence.

skills.name: usage-optimize
skills.what: Analyze token usage and cost of Claude Code work with `prompt-analytics` (local JSONL) and say what to optimize in the workflow (router sessions, cross-agent handoff, subagents, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, MCP). Use when the owner asks about cost, usage, tokens, limits, "what to optimize", or provides a CSV from `prompt-analytics export`.

agents.name: implementer
agents.what: Implements a clearly specified change (code, tests, docs) from a full brief with goal, paths, acceptance criteria and checks. Not for unclear requirements or architecture.

agents.name: planner
agents.what: High-tier planner and architect. Use for plans, architecture proposals, triage of unclear requirements and hard debugging analysis. Read-only; returns a plan with decisions, risks and acceptance checks.

agents.name: reviewer
agents.what: Independent high-tier reviewer of a diff or change against its spec and the project standard. Read-only; returns a verdict, defects and risks, not style nitpicks.

agents.name: scout
agents.what: Cheap read-only searcher. Use for finding code, collecting facts from many files, summarising logs, checking whether something exists. Returns a short conclusion, not dumps.

tools.what: Zip the global Claude Code and Codex configuration (never credentials) before any config change.
Build INDEX.json (the map agents read first) from frontmatter, SKILL.md files and tool docstrings.
Fail when tracked files contain private references: user paths or patterns from local/sensitive-patterns.txt.
Marker header for generated files: `GENERATED by sox install from <sources>; hash=<sha256 of the body>`.
Lists improvements from docs/IMPROVEMENTS.json whose machine check fails on this computer.
Install SocratexAI as the global AI core for Claude Code and Codex on this machine.
Read single fields from a big JSON file instead of dumping the whole file into the agent context.
Score the risk of a change from its diff and pick a verification level.
Append one task outcome to audits/routing_log.jsonl (the router feedback loop).
Read audits/routing_log.jsonl and propose routing changes (the LEARNED half of the loop).
Learnings log for skills: the capture half of the self-improving skill loop.
Shared helper for machine output that lives in `state/` (outside git), so `local/` holds only owner settings.
Reference packs of other agent toolkits: download on request, pin, bump and search (read-only, never run).
Update SocratexAI and the reference packs as two independent steps.
Shared pipeline engine helpers: registry loading, git change ranges, chunking, select and fix script execution, run log.
Shared pipeline engine: chunk changed files, run registry checkers, merge findings, apply fixes in at most 2 rounds.
Merger of the review pipeline: combines per-checker result files into one schema-validated findings.json.
Tiny helpers shared by the select scripts: read the request from stdin, emit candidates as JSON.
Detect full-line comments that are commented-out code or merely repeat the next code line (shared by select and fix).
Fix script for the comments checker: delete commented-out code and comments that repeat the code (idempotent).
Aggregator report: renders findings.json as a short Polish UCE report (result line, emoji bullets, one question).
Review pipeline CLI: runs the shared engine (modules/engine) with modules/stages/review/checkers.json and prints the UCE report.
Select for the comments checker: mechanical dead-code and repeating comments, plus comments left for the model.
Tier-script checker for leaks: applies the modules/tools/scripts/check_leaks.py patterns to changed lines, no model involved.
Select for readability, architecture and contracts: cheap diff-grep and AST heuristics that pick candidates for a model.
Select for test-necessity: Python tests without any assertion and tests whose body duplicates an earlier test.
Config resolver: merges layered config files, validates them and records where every value came from.
Extension registry: manifests of plugins, MCP servers, mods, skills and reference packs, and the `sox ext` actions.
Render docs/FLOW.md (Polish): the main flow table, layer order, sox commands and directory map, from the real data.
Project knowledge hub: layout of local/projects and local/groups, project keys, `sox context` and `sox project ...`.
Schema migrations for the config files that carry `schema_version` (`sox migrate`).
`sox project check | init | explain`: audit a project against the current SocratexAI setup and onboard it.
Redirect shims at the old tools/<name>.py paths, kept for projects that still call $SOCRATEX_HOME/tools/....
Generated install targets: targets/claude/* and targets/codex/* (build output, gitignored, never edited by hand).
sox: the SocratexAI command line (config, index, modules; more subcommands register in COMMANDS).
sox backup also saves the knowledge kept only in local/ (spec decision 12), and restores it.
Tests for the cleanup phase: sox state/backup/test/migrate, checker provenance, flow `needs`, routing config keys.
Tests for core/core.py (config resolver) and core/sox (CLI).
Tests for the extension registry (core/extensions.py, `sox ext`): manifests, layers, add, enable, install, startup budget.
Tests for the flow table, adapters, preference indexes and the initializer budget (core/core.py, core/sox).
Tests for `sox flow doc`: docs/FLOW.md is generated from defaults/flow.json, the parser help and the directory map.
Tests for the project knowledge hub: group layer, project.json, `sox context`, `sox project init|list|show|check|adopt`.
Tests for module manifests (modules/**/module.json), their schema and the index generated from them.
No living file may point to a path the restructure removed or moved (history in docs/specs and the shims excepted).
Tests for `sox project check | init | explain` (core/project_check.py, defaults/project-check.json). Fixtures live in temp dirs.
Tests for core/safety.json, the guard that reads it, owner-only relaxations, `config show` and the safety log.
Tests for the tools/ redirect shims and `sox shims`: forwarding, usage log, failure silence, template drift.
Tests for generated targets (markers, hand-edit detection), `sox install --plan/--check/--yes` and startup.load_rules.
Claude Code PreToolUse hook: deterministic guard for rules that have zero exceptions.

modules.name: engine
modules.what: Shared pipeline engine: chunks changed files, runs registry checkers, merges findings into one schema-validated file
modules.when: Never directly: the review and planning stages call it

modules.name: gpt
modules.what: ChatGPT conversation tools: extract a public share page and search local conversation exports
modules.when: When the owner pastes a chatgpt.com/share link or asks to search an exported ChatGPT archive

modules.name: memory
modules.what: Learning memory: skill learnings log and the ledger of named AI improvements with machine checks
modules.when: When the owner corrects a skill, and when checking which ledger improvements fail on this machine

modules.name: routing
modules.what: Model routing: tier table, risk scoring of a diff, outcome log and routing proposals, tier agents
modules.when: Before delegating (risk score), after each commit (log) and when tuning the rules (stats)
entry: python modules/tools/scripts/routing_log.py --type implementation --tier standard --agent implementer --effort medium --first-pass yes --fixes 0 --escalated no --commit HEAD

modules.name: planning
modules.what: Planning pipeline: research of unknowns and a consistency check of owner answers against the plan
modules.when: After the owner answered the question form and a plan exists, before implementation starts

modules.name: review
modules.what: Review pipeline: micro-checkers for comments, leaks, quality and test necessity, merged into one short report
modules.when: After a change is done and before the commit, to catch defects with cheap deterministic checks first

modules.name: core
modules.what: The sox command line and the core resolver: layered config, adapters, preferences index, flow table, initializer, project audit and onboarding (sox project), named safety rules, generated install targets
modules.when: Reading the effective config (with the checker overrides per stage) or the flow table at the start of a task, checking flow references and step dependencies, rotating or adopting state logs, migrating config schema versions, backing up the agent config, running the test suite, regenerating the index, planning or applying the agent config install (sox install), relaxing a safety rule, auditing or onboarding a project (check, init, explain)

modules.name: extensions
modules.what: Extension registry: manifests of plugins, MCP servers, mods, skills and read-only reference packs, with sox ext (list, show, add, enable, disable, remove, install)
modules.when: Choosing or evaluating a plugin, tool, mod or reference pack, enabling one per project, or looking up what is already known about it before proposing it again

modules.name: scripts
modules.what: Maintenance scripts: install, backup, update, leak check, index, state helper, reference packs; tools/ holds redirect shims for external callers
modules.when: Installing or updating the core, before changing agent config (backup), before a push (leaks), after editing docs or manifests (index)
